reason: The Hebrew people explicitly voice criticism against Moses, their leader. After witnessing the Egyptian army pursuing them, the Israelites cry out in fear and then directly address Moses with accusations: 'What have you done to us? Why did you bring us out to die in the wilderness?' (וַיּ֨וֹאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה... מַה־ זֹּאת עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ). They further complain that they previously told Moses to let them serve Egypt, as it would have been better than dying in the desert. This constitutes clear, direct criticism of their leader's decisions and judgment.
